recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is. Revisit only if a future FHIR-I decision changes multi-resource Subscription filter semantics.
issue_request: FHIR-30383 was a Published/Persuasive R5 FHIR-I change request asking for clearer Subscription.filterBy behavior when multiple resource triggers are present, specifically that all applicable filters must match with an example showing the behavior.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied by 8bfd3a8a002530fb2843e2b46e0a34ce6d560d7a, which changed the Subscription.filterBy definition to evaluate only conditions applicable to the resource and added framework narrative explaining resource-specific filters and the all-applicable-filters-match rule.
additional_context: The originating January 2021 Zulip discussion distinguishes AND behavior for multiple filters on one resource trigger from separate evaluation of multiple resource triggers. The block-vote/connectathon trail includes FHIR-30383, and later Subscription edits such as the resourceType-to-resource rename preserved the same semantics.
reconciliation: No source change was made. source/fhir.ini lists Subscription as active, source/hierarchy.xml includes subscriptions.html, and current source/subscription/structuredefinition-Subscription.xml plus source/subscriptions.html already contain the requested clarification.

related_jiras.note: Later Subscription filter documentation work preserved the multi-resource filter discriminator semantics and is already represented on the combined branch.
Later renamed Subscription.filterBy.resourceType to Subscription.filterBy.resource without changing the FHIR-30383 behavior; already represented on the combined branch.
